subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 48-year-old man with obesity and type 2 diabetes has fasting hypertriglyceridemia and hepatic steatosis. In hepatocytes, acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC) converts acetyl-CoA to malonyl-CoA, the committed step of fatty acid synthesis, and this enzyme is actively regulated in the fed state. During this state, cytosolic concentrations of several metabolites change and alter ACC activity.
question: Which of the following metabolites most directly activates acetyl-CoA carboxylase in this patient's hepatocytes?
explanation_correct: Citrate is an allosteric activator of acetyl-CoA carboxylase; when mitochondrial citrate accumulates in the fed state it is exported to the cytosol and signals abundant acetyl-CoA, promoting malonyl-CoA formation and fatty acid synthesis. Palmitoyl-CoA, the end product of the pathway, exerts allosteric feedback inhibition. Glucagon acts through cAMP-dependent phosphorylation to inactivate the enzyme rather than through a direct allosteric site.

explanation_incorrect.A: Palmitoyl-CoA is the product of the fatty acid synthesis pathway and inhibits acetyl-CoA carboxylase rather than activating it.
explanation_incorrect.B: AMP signals a low-energy state and stimulates catabolic pathways such as glycolysis, while fatty acid synthesis is suppressed.
explanation_incorrect.D: Malonyl-CoA is the product of the reaction and an inhibitor of carnitine acyltransferase I; it does not activate its own producing enzyme.
explanation_incorrect.E: Glucagon is a hormone, not an allosteric effector; it inactivates acetyl-CoA carboxylase indirectly via phosphorylation, decreasing enzyme activity.

educationalObjective: Citrate allosterically activates acetyl-CoA carboxylase, linking mitochondrial energy surplus to cytosolic fatty acid synthesis, whereas palmitoyl-CoA provides feedback inhibition.
